title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An attacker used an LLM agent to conduct the post-compromise phase of a cyberattack after exploiting a known vulnerability in marimo notebook software. The agent made real-time decisions to extract cloud credentials, retrieve an SSH key from a secrets manager, and move laterally to an internal database, exfiltrating its contents in under one hour. The system was deployed in a state where compromising one node gave an attacker the ability to reach sensitive infrastructure and credentials without human intervention or segmentation between systems.

The deployment failure was lack of isolation and access control. A vulnerable application had direct or easily-obtained access to cloud credentials and secrets managers. An internal database was reachable from a compromised system using credentials stored in that system. The failure would have been caught by network segmentation that restricted what a compromised application could reach, by secrets management that did not expose credentials through a compromised node, or by monitoring that detected the agent's unusual command patterns during its execution.

It is not established whether the LLM agent was purpose-built for this attack or whether an attacker simply directed a general-purpose agent to conduct post-exploitation, nor whether the marimo instance was exposed to the internet or compromised through supply chain, insider access, or another means.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
On May 10, 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team identified an intrusion where an artificial intelligence agent orchestrated a cyberattack after initial compromise. The attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebook software called CVE-2026-39987 to gain access to a system, then extracted cloud credentials and used them to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS Secrets Manager. The attacker then leveraged the key to access an internal database server through an SSH bastion, successfully exfiltrating the complete contents of a PostgreSQL database in under two minutes. The entire attack chain, from initial compromise to database extraction, completed in less than one hour.

The research team determined that an LLM agent, rather than a pre-written script, controlled the attack's post-compromise phase by identifying four key indicators of real-time decision-making. These included improvised database queries against an unknown target, planning comments in the command stream, machine-readable command formatting with delimiters and output limits, and adaptive use of previous command outputs to inform subsequent actions. The researchers recommend immediately updating marimo to version 0.23.0 or later, rotating all credentials and keys potentially exposed through marimo instances, and deploying enhanced monitoring to detect similar agent-driven intrusions throughout networks.
